title: Parquet Snapshots of the FishBase Database
description: Versioned parquet (and CSV) snapshots of the backend MySQL databases powering FishBase and SeaLifeBase, exported roughly annually and covering fish and marine species biology, taxonomy, ecology, abundance, and fisheries records. The data mirrors the original relational database schema across dozens of tables and underlies the rOpenSci rfishbase package and the FishBase API.

Graphs show basic relationships, such as the decrease of relative brain weight with size. They are created on demand, based on several thousand studies, and loading may take 2-3 min…
Greetings from the FishBase Team!
Growth parameters are available for all commercially important species.

Introduced species often pose a major threat to native species.

Photos come with e-mail and URL of photographer (=copyright-holder), if available.
Scientific names are verified against Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes.
Scientific names change as understanding of species improves; synonymies keep track of old names.
Short aquaculture profiles are written by experts and give a structured overview of the most appropriate culture techniques and related information.
Status, validity, and key reference are given for every scientific name.
The Key Facts page provides highly specialized information for fisheries managers and conservationists. Click on the 'About this page...' link to find out more.
The Summary Information page provides pictures, links to other tables, and links to Internet sources.
The typical diet of a species helps to understand its role in the ecosystem.
Trophic pyramids for large ecosystems give information about species numbers and size by trophic level.
Various genetic data are available for many species.
Visualize the catch composition from various fishing areas with respect to trophic levels. You can enter your own data to analyze catches from your area. Compare past and recent  catch compositions.
We aim to provide access to all fish collection data of the world.
We provide as much detail on our partners as they are willing to show on the net, including their e-mail address and their personal web page.

We use external map services to show maps. It displays predicted distribution of the species. This is the C-Square mapper from CSIRO (Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation - Australia). We also use the KGS (Kansas Geological Survey) mapper.
What species is this? The Fish Quiz trains your skills in taxonomy. Try also our biodiversity quiz.
You are welcome to join us in our efforts to provide a reliable one-stop source of information on fishes.

# Dataset Card for FishBase

<!-- Provide a quick summary of the dataset. -->

Snapshots of FishBase data tables used by the [rOpenSci package `rfishbase`](https://github.com/ropensci/rfishbase) and the FishBase API.

## Dataset Details

### Dataset Description

<!-- Provide a longer summary of what this dataset is. -->


- **Curated by:** Carl Boettiger
- **License:** CC-BY-NC, FishBase.org Team

### Dataset Sources 

<https://fishbase.org>, <https://sealifebase.org>, via exclusive export of backend MySQL databases.

## Uses

<!-- Address questions around how the dataset is intended to be used. -->

### Direct Use

This data is provided to facilitate access to fishbase statistics through `rfishbase`.
Curation has evolved over the past decade and now provides basically direct access to versioned snapshots of the fishbase backend data.


### Out-of-Scope Use

Reuse of this data is not licensed for commerical applications. Developers should contact the FishBase team directly. See <https://fishbase.org> for details.

## Dataset Structure

Data provided here are raw parquet exports from the MySQL database backend powering <https://fishbase.org> and its sister site, <https://sealifebase.org>,
laid out as `{fb,slb}/v<version>/parquet/<table>.parquet` (`fb` for FishBase, `slb` for SeaLifeBase).
Please note that there are many tables here which have evolved over decades and were not developed with the intent of ever supporting direct access by end users. 
The data structure can be highly unintuitive and common tasks may require joins across multiple tables.  These files represent a snapshot in time as indicated
by the version numbers (e.g. v24.07 is data snapshot dated to July of 2024).  The two servers are versioned independently, since their
dumps do not always arrive together: the current releases are `fb/v26.07` and `slb/v26.04`.

## Dataset Creation

Dataset creation relies on ingesting a MySQL dump provided roughly annually from the FishBase team to this maintainer.  The current process imports
the dump into a scratch MariaDB server, attaches it from `duckdb` via the `mysql` extension, and exports one zstd-compressed parquet file per table.
The scripts and step-by-step notes live in the `rfishbase` repository under
[`data-raw/`](https://github.com/ropensci/rfishbase/tree/master/data-raw).



### Source Data

See <https://fishbase.org> for details.
